questions.stem:
The discrete random variable $X$ has the following probability distribution

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & 2 & 4 & 7 & 10\\ \hline \mathrm{P}(X=x) & a & b & 0.1 & c\\ \hline\end{array}$

where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are probabilities.

The cumulative distribution function of $X$ is F($x$) and F(3) = 0.2 and F(6) = 0.8

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the value of $a$, the value of $b$ and the value of $c$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) F(3) = P($X$=2) so $a = 0.2$ B1
F(6) = P($X$=2) + P($X$=4) so $a+b=0.8$ so $b=0.6$ B1
Sum of probs = 1 implies $c = 0.1$ B1ft
Notes: 1st B1 for $a=0.2$; 2nd B1 for $b=0.6$; 3rd B1ft for $c=0.1$ or a value of $c$ so that their $a+b+c=0.9$ provided $a,b,c$ are probabilities. The labels may not be explicit but it must be clear which is which.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Write down the value of F(7).
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) F(7) = F(6) + 0.1 or $a+b+0.1$ or $1-c$ = $0.9$ B1
Note: B1 for 0.9 only (no ft). If their answer is based on their values of $a$, $b$ or $c$, these values must be probabilities and have $a+b=0.8$ or $c=0.1$. Just stating 0.9 with no justification is B1.

questions.stem:
The random variable $Y$ has a normal distribution with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$
The P($Y>17$) = 0.4

Find

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) [P($\mu<Y<17$)=] $0.5-0.4 = 0.1$ B1
Note: B1 for 0.1 as clearly their final answer or clear statement "P($\mu<Y<17$) = 0.1". Ignore poor or incorrect notation if answers are correct.

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) P($Y>\mu-\sigma$) = P($Z>-1$) M1
= 0.841(3) A1
P($\mu-\sigma<Y<17$) = 0.8413 - 0.4 dM1
= $0.441(3)$ A1
Notes: 1st M1 for an attempt to standardise $\mu-\sigma$ allow $\pm\frac{(\mu-\sigma)-\mu}{\sigma}$ can be un-simplified.
1st A1 for 0.841 or better (calc 0.84134473...) or $1-0.8413...=0.1587$ (accept 0.159). Sight of 0.841(3) or 0.1587 or 0.159 (or better) scores M1 A1. May be statement e.g. P($Y>\mu-\sigma$) = 0.841(3) or on clearly labelled diagram.
2nd dM1 (dep on 1st M1) for a correct use of their 0.8413 and the given 0.4, or $0.341(3)+$ their (a), or $0.6-$ their 0.1587.
2nd A1 for 0.441 or better (correct answer only 4/4).
ALT: Standardise $\mu-\sigma$ (and may get $z=-1$) scores 1st M1 as in scheme. P($Y>17$) = 0.4 $\Rightarrow Z=\left[\frac{17-\mu}{\sigma}\right]=0.25(33471...)$ so need P($-1<Z<0.25$) dM1. Sight of P($-1<Z<0.253...$) also scores 1st A1 (need 0.253 or better) = $0.441(3)$ 2nd A1. NB Just standardising and getting 0.2533 etc is no use unless it is part of a correct probability statement that would lead to the final answer.

questions.stem:
A bag contains 64 coloured beads. There are $r$ red beads, $y$ yellow beads and 1 green bead and $r+y+1=64$

Two beads are selected at random, one at a time without replacement.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the probability that the green bead is one of the beads selected.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) P($G_1$) + P($R_1\cap G_2$) + P($Y_1\cap G_2$) or P($GY$) + P($GR$) + P($RG$) + P($YG$) (o.e.) M1
$=\frac{1}{64}+\frac{r}{64}\times\frac{1}{63}+\frac{y}{64}\times\frac{1}{63}=\frac{1}{64}+\frac{r+y}{64\times63}$ or $2\times\frac{r+y}{64\times63}$ A1
$=\frac{1}{64}+\frac{63}{64\times63}$ or $\frac{2\times63}{64\times63}$ or $\frac{1}{64}+\frac{1}{64}$ or M1
$=\frac{1}{32}$ or 0.03125 A1
Notes: 1st M1 for at least 2 correct cases. May be in symbols or probs. May be in tree diagram. Use of $r=16$ or $y=47$ can score maximum of 1st M1 then A0M0A0. 1st A1 for all cases and their associated probs added. 2nd M1 for combining probabilities and using $r+y=63$. 2nd A1 for $\frac{1}{32}$ or an exact equivalent (correct answer only 4/4).

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The probability that both of the beads are red is $\frac{5}{84}$

(b) Show that $r$ satisfies the equation $r^2-r-240=0$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) P($R_1\cap R_2$) $=\frac{r}{64}\times\frac{r-1}{63}=\frac{5}{84}$ M1A1
$r(r-1)=5\times64\times63\div84=240$ hence $r^2-r-240=0$ or $r^2-r=240$ A1cso
Notes: M1 for $\frac{r}{64}\times g(r)=...$ where $g(r)$ is any linear function of $r$. 1st A1 for any correct equation in $r$. 2nd A1cso for correctly simplifying to the given equation with no incorrect working seen. There should be at least 1 intermediate step seen.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Hence show that the only possible value of $r$ is 16
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $r^2-r-240=(r-16)(r+15)\{=0\}$ or $16^2-16-240=256-256$ or $\frac{16}{64}\times\frac{15}{63}=\frac{5}{84}$ M1
so $r=16$ and rejecting $-15$ A1cso
Notes: M1 for correct factors or completing square or use of formula or substitution. A1cso for concluding $r=16$ and rejecting $-15$ (e.g. crossing out etc).

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Given that at least one of the beads is red, find the probability that they are both red.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) P($\geqslant1$ red) = P($RG$) + P($GR$) + P($RY$) + P($YR$) + P($RR$) or $\frac{2}{252}+\frac{2y}{252}+\frac{15}{252}$ (o.e.) M1
or P($R_1$) + P($R_1'\cap R_2$) or $\frac{16}{64}+\frac{48}{64}\times\frac{16}{63}$ or $1-\frac{48}{64}\times\frac{47}{63}$, $=\frac{37}{84}$ A1
Require: $\frac{P(R_1\cap R_2)}{P(\text{at least one red})}=\frac{\frac{5}{84}}{\text{"}\frac{37}{84}\text{"}}$, $=\frac{5}{37}$ or 0.1\dot{3}\dot{5} M1, A1
Notes: 1st M1 for a correct expression for at least one red. May be in symbols or probs. or in a tree. 1st A1 for $\frac{37}{84}$ (o.e.) as a single fraction or awrt 0.440 [May be implied by correct answer]. 2nd M1 for a ratio of probabilities (denom may be in symbols) with numerator of $\frac{5}{84}$ (o.e.). 2nd A1 for $\frac{5}{37}$ or an exact equivalent.

questions.stem:
Farmer Adam grows potatoes. The weights of potatoes, in grams, grown by Adam are normally distributed with a mean of 140 g and a standard deviation of 40 g.

Adam cannot sell potatoes with a weight of less than 92 g.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the percentage of potatoes that Adam grows but cannot sell.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
[$W\sim\mathrm{N}(140,40^2)$]
(a) P($W<92$) = P$\left(Z<\frac{92-140}{40}\right)$ = [P($Z<-1.2$)] M1
$=1-0.8849$ dM1
= awrt $11.5$ (%) or $0.115$ A1
Notes: 1st M1 for standardising attempt with 92 or 188, 140 and 40 (o.e.) Accept $\pm$ ignore inequality. 2nd dM1 dependent on 1st M1, for attempting $1-p$ where $0.5<p<1$. A1 for awrt 11.5 (%) or 0.115.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Condone poor use of notation etc e.g. "P > $q_1$" for P($W > q_1$) etc

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The upper quartile of the weight of potatoes sold by Adam is $q_3$

(b) Find the probability that the weight of a randomly selected potato grown by Adam is more than $q_3$
(2)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the lower quartile, $q_1$, of the weight of potatoes sold by Adam.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) P($W<q_1|W>92$) = 0.25 or P($W>q_1|W>92$) = 0.75 M1
P($92<W<q_1$) = $0.25\times0.8849=$"0.221.." or P($W>q_1$) = $0.75\times0.8849=0.663675$ M1
P($W<q_1$) = $0.221225+0.115=$ awrt $\mathbf{0.336}$ or P($W>q_1$) = $0.663675=$ awrt $\mathbf{0.664}$ A1
$\frac{q_1-140}{40}=-0.42$ (calculator gives $-0.422513\sim-0.423404$) M1
so $q_1=123.2=$ awrt $\mathbf{123}$ (g) A1
Notes: 1st M1 for a correct conditional prob. statement with $q_1$, 92 and 0.25 or 0.75. 2nd M1 for either correct probability statement and 0.25 or 0.75 $\times(1-\text{their (a)})$. 1st A1 for P($W<q_1$) = awrt 0.336 or P($W>q_1$) = awrt 0.664 NB May be standardised. Award M1M1A1 for either probability clearly stated or marked on a correct sketch. 3rd M1 for standardising with $q_1$, 140 and 40 and setting equal to $z$ where $0.40<|z|<0.45$. 2nd A1 for awrt 123 (condone minor slips in working if correct answer obtained).

parts.label: d
parts.text:
Betty selects a random sample of 3 potatoes sold by Adam.

(d) Find the probability that one weighs less than $q_1$, one weighs more than $q_3$ and one has a weight between $q_1$ and $q_3$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) $\frac{1}{4}\times\frac{1}{4}\times\frac{1}{2}\times3!$ M1M1
$=\frac{3}{16}$ or 0.1875 A1
Notes: 1st M1 for $0.25\times0.25\times0.5$ (o.e.) e.g. $\frac{1}{32}$ may be seen as decimals or fractions. 2nd M1 for $\times3!$ or $\times6$ or adding all 6 cases. Must be multiplying probabilities. A1 for $\frac{3}{16}$ or any exact equivalent.
